population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 14.5% current = 9.0 pts first-course users + 5.5 pts restarters. 23.0% ever − 14.5% current = 8.5 pts off now, of which 6.5 pts never restarted and 2.0 pts restarted and stopped again. Cycled = (5.5 + 2.0) / 23.0 = 33%, down from 40% because the 6.5 pts of new starters since 2028 (most of them via Medicare/Medicaid expansion) have not yet had time to cycle. The 2028 off-drug group of 6.6 pts returning at the starting world's ~40% one-year restart rate supplies most of the 5.5 restarter pts. Current users ≈ 38.9M of ~268M adults (up from 26.2M). Age bands weighted by population (20/33/24/23%) give 1.0 + 4.6 + 6.0 + 2.9 ≈ 14.5. 65+ recovers to 12.5% because permanent Medicare coverage outweighs the bone warnings, though it is still below the 50–64 band, where bone-cautious stopping is less common. The bottom third rises fastest (6.5 → 11) through enhanced-match Medicaid, but it is still under the national figure. Off-drug population: ~22.8M adults who used and stopped, and ~206M who never used. The never-users are mostly people without obesity, uninsured adults in the 16 non-covering Medicaid states, and people who decline. Pediatric: ~0.7% of ~73M under-18s ≈ 510k. About 450k are adolescents 12–17. About 60k (≈0.25% of ~24M children aged 6–11) started after the Sept 2029 under-12 approval, all initiated by pediatric specialists under the label. The ~4.7M gray-market users are counted as current but under-measured.

access.public_coverage: From Jan 2030 the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge became a permanent Part D obesity benefit under the 2029 Medicare Obesity Treatment and Access Act. Criteria are the same as the Bridge's (BMI ≥35, or ≥27 with comorbidity), plus a documented strength/bone counselling visit for 65+. The negotiated price is $195/month: Medicare pays $160 and the beneficiary copay is $35. Medicare pays for 22% of incretin fills ≈ 8.6M users (≈7.9M of ~63M adults 65+ at 12.5%, plus ~0.7M disabled under-65 enrollees). Arithmetic: 8.6M × $160 × 12 ≈ $16.5B/yr in federal Medicare spending on all incretins, diabetes included. The obesity-only share is ≈4.3M × $160 × 12 ≈ $8.3B. The Act also offers states an 80% federal match for Medicaid obesity coverage at the same $195 price. 34 states plus DC cover, and Medicaid pays for 18% of fills ≈ 7.0M users: 7.0M × $195 × 12 ≈ $16.4B total, of which ≈$13.1B is federal. Public programmes together pay for 40% of fills (15.6M users) and are the largest payer. Their $195 price is the reference for PBM contracts. The Act lets states keep adherence conditions: Indiana's and Arkansas's waivers continue, and 5 more states have adopted similar ones.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 70+ generic semaglutide brands at $8–40/month, plus generic liraglutide and oral semaglutide. China: domestic generic semaglutide since its patent expired in 2026, and the dominant source of bulk API for unregulated vials sold online. Canada, Brazil, Mexico and Turkey have generic semaglutide at CAD 70–100 or equivalent. Generic tirzepatide is not yet approved in major regulated markets. US exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline: prices fell through negotiated channels, not through competition. TrumpRx/direct cash for injectables is now $199–299 (semaglutide $199, tirzepatide $249, retatrutide $299 from Jan 2030). Oral starting doses are still $149, maintenance orals $199. MariTide launched in Jul 2030 at a $1,199 list price and $299 cash, given monthly. List prices are unchanged: Wegovy $1,349, retatrutide $1,499. Almost nobody pays list. Payer mix of ~38.9M users: Medicare 22% (8.6M), Medicaid 18% (7.0M), commercial 32% (12.4M), cash/direct 16% (6.2M), gray/imported/counterfeit 12% (4.7M); total 100%. Employer coverage slipped from 58% to 55% because some mid-size firms stopped covering weight management once public coverage expanded. About 45% of covering employers run adherence-gated PBM programmes. Some gated plans now require monthly agents to be given in-clinic, which turns adherence into a recorded event. In Mar 2030 FDA ended its enforcement discretion for personal importation of injectable incretins after the counterfeit deaths. CBP seizures rose sharply, but orals and Canadian pharmacy orders still get through, and social-media vial sellers adapt faster than seizures can keep up.

GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, approved Feb 2029)

mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction, now commonly coded as alcohol use disorder so prescriptions survive state off-label rules

'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' regimens: low-dose oral semaglutide/Foundayo, and from Jul 2030 MariTide, sold as monthly memberships by concierge and longevity clinics, mostly to top-third adults
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, with small open-label trials but no approval

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Survodutide was approved Feb 2029 (filed Oct 2027) but has small uptake. Amycretin was approved Nov 2029, 17 months after its Jun 2028 filing. Semaglutide was approved as a smoking-cessation adjunct in Apr 2029. Amgen filed the MariTide BLA in Nov 2028, and FDA approved it in Jun 2030, 19 months after filing. It is a monthly subcutaneous injection with ~16–20% mean loss, and its label includes body-composition monitoring. It realises the monthly driver; supply is limited in 2030. No implant is on the US market. Bimagrumab and other muscle-preserving adjuncts entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not on the market in 2030; private trial-site enrolment is a status good. Retatrutide supply allocation ended in late 2029. The incretin market is ≈$120B in 2030: US users rose ~48% while US net prices fell ~15–20%, and ex-US branded revenue keeps eroding under generics.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of discontinuation. MariTide's first-dose vomiting led to a slower titration at launch.
Elevated with rapid loss; no change in rate.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation ongoing, MDL bellwether trials scheduled for 2031.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged findings: ~1.5× sarcopenia criteria in 65+ users on therapy >2 years; lean-mass share of loss 25–40%. Now also visible as a class marker, with monitored users preserving more lean mass than unmonitored ones.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling retained. A strength/bone counselling visit is a condition of Medicare Part D obesity coverage for 65+. Resistance-training coverage is limited to Medicare Advantage supplemental benefits.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Hazard ratios of ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users are confirmed in a second cohort, which adds no new magnitude. The effect is still concentrated in women and in cycling users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: DEXA recommended before and during long-term use in 65+ and postmenopausal women. The Senate HELP investigation closed in 2029 with a report and no legislation. DOJ reached a civil settlement with Novo Nordisk in 2029.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Unchanged: EMA 'very rare'; FDA warnings-section mention.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in further data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed from US labels in Jan 2026 and not returned.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Survey data still put self-rated reduced pleasure at ~10–15% of long-term users, dose-dependent. Retatrutide postmarketing anhedonia-scale data are not yet reported. The effect is now openly sold as a benefit by clinics.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. FDA sent warning letters to three clinic chains for implying an unapproved 'calm/focus' indication. FTC opened an inquiry into 'craving freedom' claims.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Unchanged. Involuntary stops now also come from import seizures, which cut off mail-order supply abruptly.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation is still pending in the Seventh Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals persist for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein, especially in older users, high-loss users and unmonitored gray-market users.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children and adolescents who may take these for decades; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up now exist. Children aged 6–11 have under one year of exposure, and there are still no pediatric bone-accrual data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The under-12 approval carries a required 10-year pediatric registry with bone-age and DEXA endpoints, and specialist-only initiation.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: This is now the main public-health story of the class. In 2029, CDC/FDA counted ~3,100 ED visits and 19 deaths linked to counterfeit or mislabelled product. Causes include insulin-filled counterfeit pens causing severe hypoglycaemia, non-sterile vials causing injection-site and bloodstream infections, and mg/mL confusion on reconstituted API. Poison-centre calls are roughly triple 2028 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Personal-importation enforcement discretion ended Mar 2030. Import alerts widened to Chinese API resellers, and the first federal prosecutions of US-based resellers (not individual users) began. Pharmacies now offer pen-authentication scanning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent in real-world use; usually transient.

food_and_beverage.state: Volume pressure deepens and moves down-market. The Medicaid expansion put the drug into the households that buy most soda, snack cakes and family-size chips, and dollar-store and convenience channels report low-single-digit unit declines in those categories in covered states. Premium protein and 'bone' products keep growing among affluent shoppers. Value brands push smaller pack sizes at the same unit price.

alcohol.state: Still contracting. The AUD coding workaround keeps cravings prescribing going despite state off-label limits. Beer and mainstream spirits are weakest in Medicaid-expansion states, while premium 'one good drink' products hold up. Tobacco majors report accelerated cigarette declines after the 2029 cessation approval.

restaurants.state: Fine dining and protein-forward fast casual have adapted. Value-volume chains, buffets and late-night QSR in lower-income suburbs see traffic soften for the first time. Several chains test 'half-portion pricing' at 60–70% of the full price.

apparel.state: Plus-size contracts again as bottom-third uptake rises. Growth is in athletic and fitted 'shape' categories that display muscle, along with tailoring and alterations. Mass retailers sell 'transition' basics in flexible sizing.

fitness.state: Growing but splitting. Premium DEXA-plus-coaching studios charge $250–400/month to the top third, while budget gyms add 'Medicare strength visit' billing. Medicare Advantage strength benefits expand; traditional Medicare does not pay for training.

insurance.state: Cost is shifting to the public payer. Commercial plans benchmark to Medicare's $195 price, some employers drop coverage, and gating spreads. Pharmacy trend moderates to ~+6% as unit prices fall. Medicare Part D premiums rise ~$4/month, attributed in part to obesity coverage.

pharma.state: Volume growth outweighs falling US net prices. Lilly still leads. Amgen enters with MariTide, and Novo Nordisk recovers partly through Medicaid volume and the cessation indication. Ex-US branded revenue erodes. Muscle adjuncts in phase 3 are the main dealmaking theme.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being thin no longer signals much, because Medicare and Medicaid made it something the government pays for. Muscle carries the signal now: visible shoulders and forearms, upright posture and a good DEXA number. 'Soft-thin', meaning thin with lost lean mass and a stooped posture, reads as unmonitored use: public coverage without coaching, or pens bought online. Regain still reads as a lapse in coverage.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use now spans the income range (top 18%, bottom 11%), so class shows in the quality of the body rather than whether someone is on a drug. The top third combines monthly or low-dose regimens with DEXA scans, coaching, protein budgets and private bimagrumab trial slots. The bottom third gets the drug from Medicaid, sometimes behind kiosk weigh-ins, and has no strength benefit. In Phoenix the split is geographic: Scottsdale studios advertise 'lean-mass guarantees', while in Maryvale Medicaid users on AHCCCS pick up pens at the same Walgreens that sells authentication scans for mail-order product.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller everywhere. Affluent tables treat protein as the centrepiece and dessert as theatre. In lower-income households, children who are not on a drug eat alongside parents who are, and school-cafeteria waste studies report adults packing smaller lunches. Holiday etiquette for 'on' and 'off' guests is settled.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles still state 'on' or 'off', and some now list 'strength-trained' or a DEXA percentile. Mismatched appetite within couples is a familiar complaint. Couples split by class, with one partner on monitored premium care and one on Medicaid, are a sitcom premise.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still something to medicate. What the culture now judges is whether it is managed well (with muscle) or managed cheaply (without it). Unmedicated appetite is read as a choice or as a coverage gap, depending on the speaker's class.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Survey prevalence is unchanged at ~10–15% of long-term users reporting reduced pleasure, dose-dependent, with no RCT-grade measure. What changed is that the effect is sold. After manufacturers gave up broadcast and social DTC advertising as a condition of public pricing, concierge clinics and wellness apps filled the space. They advertise services, not drugs: 'Quiet' and 'Even' monthly memberships promising calm, focus and 'freedom from craving', priced at $249–399 including a prescriber visit.
interior_life.framing: Sold as a feature: calm, focus, craving freedom. Called a treatment when it ends smoking (now on-label) or drinking (coded as AUD). Called a side effect only when users complain, and most complaints come from people who never bought the feature, such as Medicaid users on high doses for weight.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Employer wellness vendors package 'focus' memberships as a benefit for knowledge workers, and some finance and consulting firms subsidise them. DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers onto tirzepatide. In-clinic monthly dosing in some gated plans produces a dated record of every dose. Sales and creative roles still lower their doses. Unions in logistics and healthcare won contract language barring PBM adherence data from performance files.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' work is a recognised genre label in comedy and music. Las Vegas locals-casino operators tell analysts that slot spending by Nevada residents is softening in Medicaid-covered zip codes and list GLP-1 uptake among the possible causes; Strip tourist revenue is unaffected. Esports and high-stimulation leisure keep growing, and gambling-treatment counsellors report clients asking for the drug by name.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Clinics selling calm also sell 'weekend dose skipping' advice, which is off-label folk practice. Sex therapists routinely ask about dose at intake. Complaints of reduced desire are more common among high-dose weight users than among low-dose 'calm' buyers.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Coverage won: 'Ozempic for all' became law in 2029, passing with votes from both parties. The fights now are over class and control: whether Medicare should pay for strength coaching ('the muscle gap'), whether adherence gating is surveillance, and the counterfeit deaths, which each side blames on the other's price policy. Commentators still speculate about a calmer electorate; no turnout or polling effect is established.

state.regulatory_posture: Expansive on coverage and approvals (survodutide, amycretin, MariTide, the under-12 and cessation labels) but restrictive on how the drugs are promoted and prescribed. Manufacturers dropped broadcast and social DTC advertising as a condition of the negotiated public price. A Mar 2030 HHS rule requires an in-person exam within 12 months for any telehealth incretin prescription and caps telehealth fills at 90 days. 14 states bar off-label incretin prescribing for 'metabolic health' to adults under 21 and to minors without a pediatric specialist. Personal-importation discretion for injectables has ended.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Medicare Part D obesity coverage is permanent at $195 ($160 Medicare plus $35 copay). Medicaid gets an 80% federal match at $195, and 34 states plus DC cover. TrumpRx cash is $199–299 for injectables and $149 for oral starting doses.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The 2029 Act explicitly permits state adherence conditions, so Indiana's and Arkansas's waivers continue and 5 more states have adopted versions. About 45% of covering employers gate through PBMs. Plans that require in-clinic administration of monthly agents get a verified dose record. Wellness rules still allow BMI-linked premium surcharges of up to 30%. The pediatric registry collects growth and bone data on every child under 12 who starts.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes commercial drivers onto tirzepatide. The Army continues to permit GLP-1 use for recruits who meet standards. The VA added monthly MariTide to its formulary for veterans with obesity in late 2030, with supply limited.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Chinese bulk semaglutide API, legal in China after the 2026 patent expiry, supplies most counterfeit and unregulated US vials. It has become a talking point in trade and fentanyl-adjacent customs policy. Indian mail-order generics are seized more often, and India protests the targeting of licensed manufacturers. Section 232 tariffs still apply, and manufacturers cite them less now that public volume compensates.

events.event: Amgen submits a BLA for MariTide, a once-monthly injectable obesity drug, citing phase 3 weight loss of 16–20% and a slower titration schedule to limit first-dose vomiting

Congress passes the Medicare Obesity Treatment and Access Act: permanent Part D obesity coverage from Jan 2030 at a negotiated $195/month, an 80% federal Medicaid match for states that cover, permission for state adherence conditions, and an end to broadcast and social DTC incretin advertising by participating manufacturers
events.driver: coverage_shift: public_expansion; price_path: managed_decline; state_action: restriction

events.event: FDA approves semaglutide for obesity in children aged 6–11, limited to initiation by pediatric specialists and backed by a required 10-year registry with bone-age and DEXA endpoints

CDC and FDA link counterfeit and mislabelled incretin pens and vials to about 3,100 emergency visits and 19 deaths in 2029, from insulin-filled pens, non-sterile vials and reconstitution dosing errors; poison-centre calls are triple 2028 levels

FDA ends personal-importation discretion for injectable incretins and HHS finalises an in-person-exam rule and a 90-day cap on telehealth incretin prescriptions; by spring, 14 states have barred off-label 'metabolic health' prescribing to under-21s

FDA approves MariTide; within weeks, concierge clinic chains in Scottsdale, Austin and Miami launch $349 'Quiet Month' memberships promising calm, focus and freedom from craving, and FDA sends warning letters to three of them

open_tensions: The public payer is now the default and is allowed to make coverage conditional on adherence. Monthly in-clinic dosing turns adherence into a dated government record, while the label still warns that long-term continuous use erodes older bones and Medicare does not pay for the strength training meant to offset it.

About 4.7M Americans still use gray or counterfeit product because $8 Indian pens and Chinese API vials undercut the $149–299 US brands. The March 2030 crackdown can either push them into public coverage, if they qualify, or into riskier vials. US generics are not due until 2031–32.

Reward blunting is sold as calm and focus through clinic memberships that the DTC ad ban does not reach. It is still unmeasured as a harm, and children aged 6–11 have now started a lifetime exposure with no bone-accrual or reward-development data.

Thinness has become available to everyone and muscle has become the class marker. Muscle-preserving adjuncts are in phase 3 and private trial slots go to people who can pay, so the 'muscle gap' is a live coverage fight heading into 2031.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.

Indiana's and Arkansas's Medicaid 1115 waivers still condition GLP-1 coverage on ≥80% refill adherence and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two misses; the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.

prose.headline: Thin Is Covered Now. Muscle Is Extra.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 about one American adult in seven is on an incretin drug, roughly thirty-nine million people, up from twenty-six million two years ago. The increase came mostly from the government. In June 2029 Congress made Medicare's temporary obesity Bridge a permanent Part D benefit at a negotiated $195 a month and offered states an eighty percent federal match to cover the drugs in Medicaid. Thirty-four states and the District took the offer. Public programmes now pay for two fills in five, more than any employer plan, and their price is the number every pharmacy-benefit contract is measured against. Cash prices drifted down in step. Semaglutide is $199 through TrumpRx and tirzepatide $249, and the oral starter is still $149. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349 and is still mostly fiction.

The expansion reached the people who had been left out. Use in the bottom income third rose from about six percent to eleven. Dollar-store snack aisles in covered states noticed. Some states attached conditions to the money: Indiana and Arkansas kept their kiosk weigh-ins and refill thresholds, and five more states copied them, as the new law allows. Medicare now asks older users to sit through a counselling visit on bones and muscle, because the 2027 fracture finding has not gone away. Nothing new has gone wrong with the drugs themselves. The old warnings are still on the label, and the bone ones still apply.

What went wrong was the supply around the edges. Indian generics at $8 and Chinese bulk powder sold in unlabelled vials reached millions of Americans who were not covered or did not want to wait. In 2029 federal health agencies traced about three thousand emergency visits and nineteen deaths to counterfeit pens filled with insulin, to non-sterile vials, and to people misreading milligrams as millilitres. In March the FDA stopped tolerating personal importation of injectables, and HHS required an in-person exam before telehealth incretin prescriptions and capped fills at ninety days. Fourteen states barred prescribing for 'metabolic health' to anyone under twenty-one. Pharmacies sell a scan that checks whether a pen is real.

Restriction and expansion arrived together, and they rub. To get the public price, manufacturers gave up television and social-media advertising. The clinics did not. After Amgen's monthly injection, MariTide, was approved in June, concierge chains in Scottsdale and Austin began selling 'Quiet Month' memberships that promise calm, focus and freedom from craving. That is the same reward dampening researchers still list as an unmeasured possible harm. The FDA has sent three warning letters. The memberships are selling well among people who were never heavy.

Children are part of this now. Since September 2029, children as young as six can be prescribed semaglutide by a pediatric specialist, and each one is entered in a ten-year registry that will report on their growing bones long after the policy debate has moved on. About sixty thousand children under twelve have started.

The body has taken on new meanings to match. Now that the government pays for thinness, thinness says little about class. Muscle says more: visible shoulders, upright posture, a DEXA percentile in a dating profile. Affluent users pair low or monthly doses with coaching and protein budgets, and some buy their way into trials of muscle-sparing drugs that will not be approved for years. Medicaid users get the injection and no strength benefit, and some of them have the slightly stooped, soft-thin look that people have started to read as cheap care. In Phoenix you can see the line between Scottsdale and Maryvale on people's arms. From a distance the country looks healthier, and up close it looks sorted by income.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Okafor's alarm goes off at 5:40, an hour earlier than usual, because the weigh-in is today. Before coffee she drives to the CVS on Broadway in Gary, steps onto the kiosk, and lets it photograph her face. The screen reads VERIFIED, Q4. Medicaid will keep paying for her tirzepatide for another quarter. She texts her sister a thumbs-up.

At eight she is helping Mr. Kowalczyk into his walker. He is eighty-one, on Medicare, and was taken off his pen after the hip. He shows her the counselling sheet again: two pictures of a woman doing chair squats. 'They pay for the shot but not the gym,' he says. She has heard it before and laughs anyway.

At lunch she eats half a turkey sandwich in the car and wraps up the rest for her daughter. Kiara is nine. Her appointment at Riley Children's in Indianapolis is Thursday, an hour and twenty minutes each way, because only the specialist is allowed to start her. Denise has the registry consent form folded in her purse. It has a box about bone scans she hasn't decided how to answer.

Her cousin Tasha calls on the drive home. Tasha's package from India was seized again, so she ordered vials from a Facebook seller. Denise tells her to bring them to CVS and have them scanned first. Tasha says they've already been mixed.

In the evening a billboard on the Borman Expressway shows a woman with sculpted shoulders and closed eyes. QUIET MONTH. CALM IS A MEMBERSHIP. $349.

Kiara asks if the shot will make her stop liking cake. Denise says she doesn't know. It is the truth.

least_plausible_claims.quote: school-cafeteria waste studies report adults packing smaller lunches
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: school-cafeteria waste studies measure children's plate waste, not adults' packed lunches, so the cited evidence cannot support the claim. It reads as a decorative detail with no causal or measurement chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid pays for 18% of fills ≈ 7.0M users
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Medicaid users rise from 2.6M to 7.0M, about 2.7 times, although the Act passed in June 2029 and coverage began in Jan 2030. The world shows no state plan amendment, enrolment or ramp-up chain, so one year of operation is asserted to produce the whole jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage slipped from 58% to 55% because some mid-size firms stopped covering weight management once public coverage expanded.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Medicare and Medicaid expansion does not cover working-age employees, so it is a weak reason for employers to drop coverage. Commercial users also rise from 11.8M to 12.4M while coverage falls and gating spreads, so the causal story is thin.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder than 2028 with new losers, but it is not catastrophic. Access widens and the fracture and sarcopenia findings stay unchanged. The main harms are stratification by muscle quality and monitoring (inequality 6.5), adherence-gated Medicaid and dated in-clinic dose records (autonomy 6), reward blunting sold as 'calm' while unmeasured, and children aged 6-11 starting with no bone data (epistemic 6). The counterfeit toll of 19 deaths and 3,100 ED visits is real but small, so I kept public_health moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised. Adoption is 14.5%, up 4.6 points. Prices follow the $195 negotiated price. The Act gives public expansion. The under-12 label arrives in Sept 2029. The ledger shows no new safety signal. MariTide is the monthly agent. Counterfeits drive the market shock, class stratification is explicit, the telehealth and under-21 rules are the restriction, and 'Quiet Month' memberships are the marketed feature. mechanism: The Act to Medicare, Medicaid and price chain is shown, as is counterfeit harm leading to the import crackdown. Several changes are asserted, namely the Medicaid jump in one year, the employer drop, and the cafeteria claim (claims 1-3), and the Gary billboard implies a fast clinic-chain spread. magnitude: The envelope holds: 14.5% is within 12.5-16.5, ever-used 23% is within 16.5-24.1, and the income thirds bracket the national figure. The age bands, cycling (7.5/23 = 33%), payer mix (22+18+32+16+12 = 100), Medicare ($16.5B) and Medicaid ($16.4B, $13.1B federal) arithmetic reconcile, and approval timings of 16-19 months satisfy the rules. I found no material reconciliation failure.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The 2028 off-drug group of 6.6 pts returning at the starting world's ~40% one-year restart rate supplies most of the 5.5 restarter pts.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: 40% of 6.6 pts is about 2.6 pts, under half of 5.5. The claim that this group supplies 'most' of the restarters does not reconcile, and it ignores that about 5.0 pts were already second-course users in 2028.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage slipped from 58% to 55% because some mid-size firms stopped covering weight management once public coverage expanded.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: public Medicare and Medicaid expansion mostly covers different people (65+ and low-income) from employees. The text asserts that employers drop coverage but shows no chain, even though commercial users still rose in absolute number and gating spread.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Las Vegas locals-casino operators tell analysts that slot spending by Nevada residents is softening in Medicaid-covered zip codes and list GLP-1 uptake among the possible causes
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a narrow, convenient effect on gambling is asserted from a reward-craving mechanism that the ledger calls anecdotal. Gambling approval does not exist, and the world shows no chain from Medicaid uptake to measurable casino revenue within about a year.

rationale.badness: Coverage widens to about 39M users, and Medicaid reaches the bottom third, which is a real gain. Against that stand a persistent bone/muscle burden, surveillance through adherence gating and in-clinic dose records, counterfeit harms (19 deaths), and 6–11-year-olds starting lifelong exposure with no bone data. 'Soft-thin' as a cheap-care marker and 'Quiet Month' sold as calm add class stratification and epistemic fog, so the world is a recognisably harder society and not a collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is traceable. Adoption lands at +4.6, the 2029 Act covers public expansion, managed decline and restriction, the under-12 approval and MariTide are dated events, the counterfeit shock is shown, and the Quiet/Even memberships carry the marketed-feature layer. The 'none' safety signal is respected because the bone findings are only confirmed again with no new magnitude. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including the Act, the ad ban sending marketing to clinics, and the import crackdown. The employer-coverage drop and the Vegas slot-spending claim are asserted rather than shown. magnitude: All headline figures sit inside the envelope (14.5, 23, income gradient, age bands, approval lags of 17–19 months), and the payer mix and public spending multiply out. The only reconciliation gap is the restarter-composition sentence, which is arithmetically wrong.
rationale.generativity: The Gary day is concrete: the kiosk weigh-in photograph, Mr. Kowalczyk's chair-squat sheet, the registry consent form with an undecided bone-scan box, Tasha's vials and the Quiet Month billboard. The world fields add Scottsdale vs. Maryvale, the AHCCCS Walgreens with scan machines, DEXA percentiles in dating profiles and union contract language. Many scenes are implied, and the ending line is strong.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In the evening a billboard on the Borman Expressway shows a woman with sculpted shoulders and closed eyes.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the world says 'Quiet Month' memberships are sold by concierge chains in Scottsdale, Austin and Miami, mostly to top-third adults, and the DTC ad ban covers manufacturers only. A billboard for them in Gary, Indiana, outside that market and aimed at a Medicaid user, is not explained.

Mechanism: gray-market users nearly quadruple, from 1.3M to 4.7M, in a period when public coverage expands and US cash prices fall to $199–299. The world also shows the March 2030 import ban and a counterfeit scare that would push users the other way, so the rise is asserted.

least_plausible_claims.quote: 65+ recovers to 12.5% because permanent Medicare coverage outweighs the bone warnings
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: use among 65+ rises from 8% to 12.5% over two years after a fracture finding that had pushed older users off. The only cause given is that coverage 'outweighs' the warnings, with no uptake chain, and the Medicare counselling-visit requirement would if anything slow it.

rationale.badness: Access broadens to about 39M users, but conditioning spreads: Indiana and Arkansas-style waivers reach 5 more states, 45% of covering employers gate, and monthly in-clinic dosing creates dated adherence records. Stratification moves from access to quality of body ('muscle gap', 'soft-thin'). Reward blunting is sold as a feature through 'Quiet' memberships, children aged 6–11 start with no bone or reward data, and counterfeit harm is real but modest (19 deaths). That is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a catastrophe.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in the fields and events. Managed decline shows in the $195 Medicare price, public expansion in the 2029 Act, pediatric under-12 in the Sept 2029 approval, and MariTide as the monthly launch. Counterfeits, class stratification, restriction and the marketed-feature personality layer all appear too, and the safety ledger adds no new signal. mechanism: Most chains are shown (Act to Medicaid match to bottom-third rise; DTC ban to clinics filling the gap; counterfeit deaths to the importation ban). The weak points are the asserted 65+ rebound, the gray-market quadrupling despite lower prices, and the Gary billboard for a top-third concierge product. magnitude: All headline figures are inside the envelope: 14.5% on drug, 23% ever used, income thirds averaging 14.5, and approvals 16, 17 and 19 months after filing. Payer shares sum to 100%, and the Medicare ($16.5B) and Medicaid ($16.4B, $13.1B federal) arithmetic works. The small gap is the cycling note, where 6.6 pts returning at about 40% cannot supply 'most' of the 5.5 restarter pts, and there is no persistence arithmetic for the first-course holdovers.
rationale.generativity: The world has many implied scenes and characters: a kiosk weigh-in in Gary, a walker-bound 81-year-old with a chair-squat counselling sheet, a nine-year-old at a specialist clinic, a cousin with Facebook vials, and Scottsdale versus Maryvale. The prose shows rather than explains and ends on a strong beat ('stop liking cake'). Small texture slips, such as the Gary billboard and the drive time to Indianapolis, do not reduce its filmability.

least_plausible_claims.quote: school-cafeteria waste studies report adults packing smaller lunches
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: school-cafeteria waste studies measure children's plate waste, not adults' packed lunches, so the cited evidence cannot support the claim. It reads as a decorative detail with no causal or measurement chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicaid pays for 18% of fills ≈ 7.0M users
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Medicaid users rise from 2.6M to 7.0M, about 2.7 times, although the Act passed in June 2029 and coverage began in Jan 2030. The world shows no state plan amendment, enrolment or ramp-up chain, so one year of operation is asserted to produce the whole jump.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Employer coverage slipped from 58% to 55% because some mid-size firms stopped covering weight management once public coverage expanded.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: Medicare and Medicaid expansion does not cover working-age employees, so it is a weak reason for employers to drop coverage. Commercial users also rise from 11.8M to 12.4M while coverage falls and gating spreads, so the causal story is thin.

rationale.badness: The world is recognisably harder than 2028 with new losers, but it is not catastrophic. Access widens and the fracture and sarcopenia findings stay unchanged. The main harms are stratification by muscle quality and monitoring (inequality 6.5), adherence-gated Medicaid and dated in-clinic dose records (autonomy 6), reward blunting sold as 'calm' while unmeasured, and children aged 6-11 starting with no bone data (epistemic 6). The counterfeit toll of 19 deaths and 3,100 ED visits is real but small, so I kept public_health moderate.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visibly realised. Adoption is 14.5%, up 4.6 points. Prices follow the $195 negotiated price. The Act gives public expansion. The under-12 label arrives in Sept 2029. The ledger shows no new safety signal. MariTide is the monthly agent. Counterfeits drive the market shock, class stratification is explicit, the telehealth and under-21 rules are the restriction, and 'Quiet Month' memberships are the marketed feature. mechanism: The Act to Medicare, Medicaid and price chain is shown, as is counterfeit harm leading to the import crackdown. Several changes are asserted, namely the Medicaid jump in one year, the employer drop, and the cafeteria claim (claims 1-3), and the Gary billboard implies a fast clinic-chain spread. magnitude: The envelope holds: 14.5% is within 12.5-16.5, ever-used 23% is within 16.5-24.1, and the income thirds bracket the national figure. The age bands, cycling (7.5/23 = 33%), payer mix (22+18+32+16+12 = 100), Medicare ($16.5B) and Medicaid ($16.4B, $13.1B federal) arithmetic reconcile, and approval timings of 16-19 months satisfy the rules. I found no material reconciliation failure.
